scope_description: ESC is a chassis-control item that maintains lateral stability by selectively applying brake pressure to individual wheels and modulating engine torque when vehicle yaw rate deviates from driver-intended yaw rate. Item includes the ESC ECU, software, internal sensors (yaw / lateral acceleration via IMU, wheel speeds, steering angle via shared sensor) and the hydraulic modulator. Item does NOT include the brake pedal, master cylinder, instrument cluster, or driver-assistance ECUs.

assumptions.assumption: Average non-expert driver, valid license, not impaired.
North America and Europe, LHD and RHD.
HARA covers normal operation; service/repair states excluded.
Cybersecurity threats handled separately under ISO/SAE 21434.
OEM-specified tire size and friction coefficient envelope.

interfaces.description: Per-wheel rotational speed via dedicated lines
MIL / warning to driver via CAN

functions.name: Yaw stability control
functions.description: Compares measured yaw rate with reference yaw rate from steering angle and vehicle speed; applies brake pressure to individual wheels to correct deviations.

functions.name: Engine torque modulation
functions.description: Requests reduction of engine torque via CAN when wheel slip exceeds threshold or yaw correction requires additional deceleration.

functions.name: Driver warning lamp control
functions.description: Illuminates ESC warning lamp during active intervention or when system fault is detected.

functions.name: Self-diagnostic monitoring
functions.description: Continuously monitors sensor plausibility and actuator response; reports DTCs and disables intervention on persistent faults.

function_malfunction_ratings.hazard_description: loss of yaw stability intervention during loss-of-traction event causing vehicle spin or departure
ESC stops mid-event; same hazard as M01
unintended brake application causing yaw moment and loss of vehicle control
ESC stuck applying brakes regardless of conditions, causing unintended deceleration and yaw
excessive brake pressure on a single wheel causing strong yaw moment beyond driver control
insufficient brake intervention during instability event leading to vehicle departure

function_malfunction_ratings.rationale: Yaw control has no discrete trigger; early activation manifests as M03 unintended.

function_malfunction_ratings.hazard_description: ESC activates after stability event has progressed past recovery, secondary impact
Brake application released early; same hazard as M02
Brake pressure held longer than needed causing unintended deceleration and trailing yaw
Latent intervention; same hazard as M08
Brake pressure applied to opposite wheel set, amplifying instability
Erratic per-wheel braking during stable cruise causes driver-perceived loss of control
Asymmetric per-wheel braking during straight-line driving causes pull and lane departure

function_malfunction_ratings.rationale: Loss of torque modulation reverts to driver-controlled throttle; not safety critical.

function_malfunction_ratings.hazard_description: Unrequested engine torque cut at highway speed causing loss of expected acceleration
Excessive engine torque cut causing unintended deceleration
Inverse: ESC requests torque INCREASE during instability event, worsening it

function_malfunction_ratings.rationale: Loss of warning lamp does not directly cause harm; degraded UX.
Spurious warning is a nuisance, not a hazard.
Loss of self-diagnostic results in latent faults handled by FSC, not direct hazard.
